headline: Negeri Sembilan Throne: Three of the Four Undang Titles Are Now Contested
context: On 19 April 2026, four signatories, each claiming an Undang title, issued a proclamation purporting to depose Tuanku Muhriz and chose Tunku Nadzaruddin to succeed him. Tuanku Muhriz continues to carry out the Ruler's functions.

changes.summary: Correction: The declaration is now described as purporting to depose the Ruler, and the dismissal of one signatory is attributed to the Menteri Besar. Corrected who called the act menderhaka and removed the JAIS reference.
Correction: Earlier editions said four Undangs signed the declaration; Mubarak Dohak signed and read it, with the three other Undangs present.

Correction: Rewritten as of 9 November 2026, with the September decisions and the court cases. Earlier editions treated only Mubarak's title as disputed; the DKU disputes three of the four signatories' titles. Our last correction wrongly said only Mubarak signed; both sides describe four signatories. We now spell his name Thahak, as court records do.

cards.big: On 15 September the state exco backed a 19 April proclamation to depose Tuanku Muhriz. Two days later the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) called it invalid.
cards.sub: The DKU, the state's council on custom, says three of the four signatories were not lawful Undangs at the time. They say they were.

cards.big: Article X lets Undangs call on a Ruler to abdicate after a 'full and complete enquiry'. Article XXIX counts their powers as duly used when at least three act.
cards.sub: The DKU says no full enquiry was held; the AGC found no facts showing Article X was followed. The four say they held one on 5 March.

cards.big: Mubarak Thahak, who read the 19 April proclamation, proclaimed Tuanku Muhriz Ruler as Undang of Sungai Ujong in 2008.
cards.sub: On 5 June his side proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin. The DKU calls it contempt of a same-day order; the six it named say only a Special Court can hear it. A stay bid failed on 4 November.

cards.big: The DKU says Sungai Ujong's elders removed Mubarak in May 2025, Jelebu's removed Maarof Mat Rashad in May 2023, and Abdul Rahim Yasin was never installed in Rembau.
cards.sub: Article XVI(3) makes such advice final and non-justiciable. The four reject it and say they remain the Undangs.

cards.big: Article X's proclamation also needs the Menteri Besar's signature. MB Ismail Lasim signed on 3 August and later cited duress; a lawyer for the six says he signed freely.
cards.sub: On 20 September Tuanku Muhriz revoked 10 exco appointments. Ismail objected; the Attorney-General called the revocation valid.

cards.big: This was a dispute over Undangs before it became one over a Ruler. The throne now depends on who lawfully held three Undang titles on 19 April.
No side disputes that Undangs may remove a Ruler. Whether they lawfully did on 19 April is a question every side has answered and no court has.
